text:
In Hindu tradition, Triveni Sangam is a confluence (Sanskrit: sangama) of three rivers that is a sacred place, with a bath there said to flush away all of one's sins and free one from the cycle of rebirth. The best-known of these confluences is the Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj which is the site of Kumbh Mela.

--- Practical Travel Context (Wikivoyage) ---
Prayagraj (प्रयागराज Prayāgrāj), formerly Allahabad (इलाहाबाद Ilāhābād), is one of the holiest cities in India, is in Uttar Pradesh. The city is famous for being the site of the confluence of the holy rivers Ganges and Yamuna; and also the Hindu pilgrimage Kumbh Mela, the largest gathering of humans on the planet holding hundreds of millions of pilgrims every 12 years.
best_time: October to March (pleasant weather, ideal for heritage monuments, wildlife, and cultural walks)
